domains.title: Sin, Human Fall, And The Need For New Birth
domains.anchor: Romans 3:23 — "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God."

scripture.excerpt: Of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
scripture.function: The original divine command and its consequence — disobedience is not merely failure; it produces death. The entire logic of the new birth requires this foundation.

scripture.excerpt: And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil...
scripture.function: The fall: temptation, rebellion, guilt, shame, broken communion, expulsion. Every element of the new birth answers what was lost here.

scripture.excerpt: Every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
scripture.function: The pervasive inward corruption following the fall — sin is not external circumstance but the condition of the human heart apart from divine intervention.

scripture.excerpt: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.
scripture.function: Sin is not merely behavioral but constitutional — a condition requiring divine cleansing, not self-repair.

scripture.excerpt: Your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you.
scripture.function: The defining consequence of sin is separation from God — the broken relational structure that the new birth must repair.

scripture.excerpt: There is none righteous, no, not one... for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.
scripture.function: The apostolic summary of universal guilt — the doctrinal foundation from which the necessity of salvation is argued.

scripture.excerpt: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men...
scripture.function: Sin and death passed to all through Adam — refuting any view that human beings begin neutral before God.

scripture.excerpt: The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
scripture.function: Sin pays a wage of death; salvation is a gift. This contrast is foundational to understanding why the new birth is received, not earned.

scripture.excerpt: And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins...
scripture.function: The condition before salvation is spiritual death — not weakness, but death that requires God’s life-giving act in the new birth.

scripture.excerpt: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
scripture.function: The apostolic denial of human sinlessness — a corrective against any softening of the universal need for salvation.

vocabulary.definition: Rebellion against God and violation of His will, bringing guilt, corruption, and separation.
vocabulary.relevance: Defines the human problem at its root — without this definition, salvation becomes moral advice rather than rescue.

vocabulary.definition: The entrance of sin through human disobedience and the resulting ruin of human life before God.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains why the need for new birth is universal — all are affected by what was introduced in Genesis 3.

vocabulary.definition: The moral ruin and inward disorder produced by sin in human nature.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that the problem is not only what people do but what they are apart from divine intervention.

vocabulary.definition: Broken communion with God resulting from sin.
vocabulary.relevance: Makes the new birth necessary as restoration of access, not merely moral cleanup.

vocabulary.definition: God’s righteous response to sin — the real accountability that makes salvation an urgent matter.
vocabulary.relevance: Without this category, grace becomes sentiment. Judgment gives weight to the gospel proclamation.

vocabulary.definition: Real accountability before God because of sin — not merely psychological feeling but moral and legal standing.
vocabulary.relevance: Ensures that salvation is understood as actual forgiveness, not merely a change of emotional state.

vocabulary.definition: The consequence of sin in spiritual separation from God and eventual physical mortality.
vocabulary.relevance: Anchors the language of new birth in contrast to death — one must be born again because one is spiritually dead.

vocabulary.definition: The universal state of fallen humanity under sin, guilt, corruption, and separation from God.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the scope of need — every human being requires the new birth.

vocabulary.definition: The necessity of divine rescue, because human beings cannot repair their own condition before God.
vocabulary.relevance: Removes self-salvation as an option and establishes dependence on God’s revealed provision.

vocabulary.definition: The divinely revealed entrance into new-covenant life, necessary because of sin and the resulting separation.
vocabulary.relevance: Anchors the whole subject — the new birth is the necessary answer to the human condition.

domains.title: Promise, Covenant, And The Redemptive Structure Of
domains.anchor: Jeremiah 31:31, 33 — "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant... I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts."

scripture.excerpt: I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head...
scripture.function: The proto-evangelion — the first promise of divine redemption placed immediately after the fall. Every subsequent covenant promise builds toward its fulfillment.

scripture.excerpt: In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
scripture.function: The Abrahamic covenant — a global redemptive promise that shapes the scope of apostolic mission and the universality of new-covenant life.

scripture.excerpt: The blood shall be to you for a token... when I see the blood, I will pass over you.
scripture.function: The Passover establishes blood as the covenant-protection category that later reaches fulfillment in Christ’s atoning sacrifice.

scripture.excerpt: Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you.
scripture.function: Blood-covenant ratification — the category that Hebrews applies to the new covenant inaugurated through Christ’s death.

scripture.excerpt: And Aaron shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary... for all the congregation of Israel.
scripture.function: The Day of Atonement — annual sacrifice for sin’s removal that prefigures and is superseded by the once-for-all work of Christ.

scripture.excerpt: I will make a new covenant... I will put my law in their inward parts, and will be their God.
scripture.function: The great new-covenant promise: inward transformation, personal knowledge of God, complete forgiveness — the categories fulfilled in the new birth.

scripture.excerpt: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you... A new spirit will I put within you... I will put my spirit within you.
scripture.function: The prophetic promise most directly anticipating the new birth: washing, new heart, and divine Spirit indwelling — Spirit birth is its fulfillment.

scripture.excerpt: But Christ being come an high priest... by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption.
scripture.function: The new-covenant fulfillment of the entire sacrificial system — Christ’s blood achieves what the blood of animals only prefigured.

scripture.excerpt: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus... let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith.
scripture.function: Access to God through covenant blood — the new-covenant reality of which tabernacle and temple were only types.

vocabulary.definition: God’s declared intention to save and fulfill His redemptive purpose across human history.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that the new birth does not appear without preparation — it is the fulfillment of what God had been promising from Genesis onward.

vocabulary.definition: The binding relationship established by God with defined promises, obligations, and identity.
vocabulary.relevance: Places the new birth inside a structured relationship rather than an isolated experience — entry into new life is covenant entry.

vocabulary.definition: The divinely ordered offering associated with sin, cleansing, approach to God, and covenant ratification.
vocabulary.relevance: Prepares the logic of why Christ’s death is necessary — the cross is the fulfillment of a long sacrificial category.

vocabulary.definition: The covenant and redemptive category associated with life, sacrifice, atonement, and cleansing in Scripture.
vocabulary.relevance: Makes the language of remission and covenant ratification through Christ’s blood intelligible — blood was always the covenant medium.

vocabulary.definition: God’s act of removing defilement and guilt according to His ordained provision.
vocabulary.relevance: Prepares the categories of washing, remission, and purification that appear in new-birth teaching.

vocabulary.definition: God dwelling within His people by His Spirit — the culmination of His covenant purpose.
vocabulary.relevance: Contextualizes Spirit reception as the fulfillment of a long divine desire, not a new idea appearing at Pentecost without roots.

vocabulary.definition: The interconnected biblical categories that together prepare for and interpret the new birth.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents the learner from reading the new birth in isolation — it is intelligible only within this larger biblical structure.

vocabulary.definition: The realization of what God promised in redemptive relationship — when promise becomes presence and provision becomes reality.
vocabulary.relevance: Describes what happens at Pentecost and in every new birth: the promised Spirit is given and the new covenant becomes real.

vocabulary.definition: The cleansing category in both Testaments that prepares understanding for water and spiritual birth.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects Old Testament ritual washing and prophetic cleansing promises to the new-birth categories of baptism and Spirit reception.

vocabulary.definition: Approach to the divine presence made possible through divine provision rather than human effort.
vocabulary.relevance: Places the new birth in the context of restored access — what was lost in the fall is restored through the new covenant.

domains.title: The Gospel As The Basis Of New Birth
domains.anchor: 1 Corinthians 15:3–4 — "Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And... he was buried, and... he rose again the third day."

scripture.excerpt: He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
scripture.function: The prophetic foundation of substitutionary suffering — Christ’s death is not accidental but purposeful and bearing the weight of human sin.

scripture.excerpt: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice... and gave up the ghost.
scripture.function: The historical event of the crucifixion — the new birth is grounded in the death of a specific person in real history.

scripture.excerpt: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.
scripture.function: The resurrection announcement — the new birth is grounded not only in death but in the vindicated life of the risen Christ.

scripture.excerpt: Jesus of Nazareth... ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain: whom God hath raised up...
scripture.function: Peter’s Pentecost sermon: the gospel is proclaimed as specific historical events leading to the apostolic response of Acts 2:38.

scripture.excerpt: Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.
scripture.function: The double purpose of the gospel event: Christ’s death addresses sin; His resurrection addresses justification — both together form the redemptive basis.

scripture.excerpt: While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us... we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son.
scripture.function: Reconciliation through Christ’s death — the gospel resolves the problem of separation established in Domain 1.

scripture.excerpt: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?... even so we also should walk in newness of life.
scripture.function: The gospel event and the new-birth response are directly linked — apostolic response is shaped by the gospel pattern.

scripture.excerpt: I declare unto you the gospel... how that Christ died for our sins... And that he was buried, and that he rose again...
scripture.function: Paul’s definition of the gospel: three events, verified by witnesses, rooted in Scripture — the basis of all apostolic preaching.

scripture.excerpt: He died for all... God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself... he hath made him to be sin for us.
scripture.function: The substitutionary and reconciling work of Christ — the fullest Pauline statement of what the gospel accomplishes.

scripture.excerpt: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness.
scripture.function: Christ bears sin so that those who respond may live unto righteousness — the new birth is the application of what the cross achieved.

vocabulary.definition: The good news of the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ as the redemptive basis of salvation.
vocabulary.relevance: Provides the foundation the learner must stand on — the new birth is grounded in these specific historical events.

vocabulary.definition: The completed work of Christ upon which salvation rests — not human effort or sincerity but the finished work of the cross and empty tomb.
vocabulary.relevance: Distinguishes the apostolic doctrine of salvation from any system grounded in human achievement or religious performance.

vocabulary.definition: Christ’s sacrificial death for sin — bearing the guilt and penalty of human rebellion so that those who respond may receive forgiveness and new life.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains why repentance, remission, and cleansing are possible — the debt has been paid; the provision has been made.

vocabulary.definition: Christ’s real burial as part of the gospel event — a doctrinal affirmation that Christ genuinely died and was genuinely raised.
vocabulary.relevance: The burial connects the gospel to water baptism in Romans 6:3– 4 — the new-birth response corresponds to the gospel event.

vocabulary.definition: Christ’s rising from the dead in victory and vindication — the Father’s confirmation that the atoning work was accepted.
vocabulary.relevance: Without resurrection the gospel is only tragedy. The resurrection makes the new birth possible — the risen Christ pours out the Spirit.

vocabulary.definition: The completed redemptive accomplishment of Christ — upon which all apostolic proclamation depends.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that new birth is entry into something already accomplished, not a human contribution to an unfinished salvation.

vocabulary.definition: Restored relationship to God through Christ’s work — the rupture of separation repaired by the gospel.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the problem of Domain 1 (separation) to the solution (reconciliation through Christ).

vocabulary.definition: The revealed apostolic response to the finished work of Christ — the commanded form in which people enter the salvation Christ accomplished.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents the learner from seeing repentance, baptism, and Spirit reception as additions to the gospel.

vocabulary.definition: Christ bearing in His death the consequence of sin that belonged to human beings — dying in the place of the guilty.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes why the cross is not merely an example of love but a transaction of redemption.

vocabulary.definition: Christ’s triumph over death and the grave in the resurrection — the new creation breaking into the old.
vocabulary.relevance: The same life that raised Christ from the dead is the Spirit given to those who are born again.

domains.title: Repentance As Turning, Surrender, And Covenant
domains.anchor: Acts 2:38 — "Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins..."

scripture.excerpt: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD... for he will abundantly pardon.
scripture.function: The Old Testament call to repentance: turning from sin is joined to returning to God — the basic directional structure of all repentance teaching.

scripture.excerpt: Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions... Make you a new heart and a new spirit.
scripture.function: God’s prophetic call for full turning including a new heart — repentance is not surface behavior but inward orientation.

scripture.excerpt: O generation of vipers... Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance.
scripture.function: John the Baptist establishes that repentance has visible fruit — the presence of changed direction is the evidence that turning is real.

scripture.excerpt: Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
scripture.function: Christ’s stark declaration of the necessity of repentance — not as option for the especially sinful but as universal requirement.

scripture.excerpt: Repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations.
scripture.function: The risen Christ commissions the apostolic proclamation of repentance as a global mission — repentance belongs to the center of the apostolic message.

scripture.excerpt: What shall we do? Then Peter said unto them, Repent...
scripture.function: Repentance is the first commanded response to the gospel at Pentecost — it stands at the opening of the apostolic new-birth proclamation.

scripture.excerpt: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.
scripture.function: Repentance leads to conversion and the blotting out of sins — directed, purposeful, and producing real results before God.

scripture.excerpt: God... now commandeth all men every where to repent: Because he hath appointed a day in which he will judge the world.
scripture.function: Paul’s global call to repentance before judgment — universal, urgent, and doctrinally serious.

scripture.excerpt: Godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
scripture.function: The distinction between godly sorrow (producing real repentance) and worldly sorrow (producing only regret) — the standard for evaluating whether repentance is genuine.

scripture.excerpt: Repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
scripture.function: Paul’s summary of the apostolic message: repentance directed to God, producing works that evidence its reality.

vocabulary.definition: Turning from sin to God in surrender, confession, and obedient response — the necessary beginning of apostolic salvation response.
vocabulary.relevance: Defines the domain’s central category; must be distinguished from emotional regret, behavior modification, or vague spiritual openness.

vocabulary.definition: Decisive movement away from sin and toward God — the directional structure of repentance.
vocabulary.relevance: Captures the active, directional nature of repentance — it is not merely stopping sin but actively orienting toward God.

vocabulary.definition: Sorrow produced by the Spirit that leads to genuine repentance and real change — distinguished from worldly sorrow that produces only regret.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains the internal dynamic of repentance — it begins with conviction but must move to turning to qualify as true repentance.

vocabulary.definition: Honest acknowledgment of sin before God — a component of repentance that corresponds to the reality of guilt.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents repentance from being vague; the person who has truly repented has honestly named their sin before God.

vocabulary.definition: Rejection of sin, false allegiance, and rebellion in favor of God’s rule.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that repentance involves active rejection, not passive drift away from sin.

vocabulary.definition: Yielding self-rule to God’s authority — the response to the recognition that sin is rebellion against God’s rightful lordship.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects repentance to the doctrine of sin established in Domain 1 — if sin is rebellion, then repentance is yielded return.

vocabulary.definition: Spirit-given awareness of sin and need for response — the internal work that prepares repentance.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains the dynamic between Spirit-given conviction and human response.

vocabulary.definition: Corrective action where required by genuine repentance — making right what can be made right.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents repentance from remaining purely internal; where sin has caused harm, genuine repentance seeks to repair it.

vocabulary.definition: Obedient turning that prepares entry into revealed new- covenant life — repentance as the beginning of apostolic salvation response.
vocabulary.relevance: Places repentance inside the covenant structure of Domain 2 — it is the beginning of the response that leads into covenant belonging.

vocabulary.definition: Outward fruit showing inward turning — the behavioral change that evidences real repentance.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the internal reality of repentance to its external evidence; distinguishes real repentance from claimed repentance without fruit.

domains.title: Water Baptism And Apostolic Gospel Response
domains.anchor: Acts 2:38 — "Be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins..."

scripture.excerpt: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness... will I cleanse you.
scripture.function: The prophetic promise of divine cleansing through water — preparing the baptism-Spirit structure of the new birth that Ezekiel’s context joins to Spirit indwelling.

scripture.excerpt: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
scripture.function: Christ’s commission joins belief and baptism in the same salvation statement — baptism is not detached from the faith that saves.

scripture.excerpt: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
scripture.function: Christ’s own statement that new-birth entry requires both water and Spirit — the two dimensions of new-covenant entry the apostles later command.

scripture.excerpt: Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
scripture.function: The apostolic inaugural command — baptism commanded, named, and tied to remission in the first public new-birth proclamation.

scripture.excerpt: Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
scripture.function: Baptism described as washing away sins — the cleansing language establishes that baptism carries real doctrinal meaning, not empty symbolism.

scripture.excerpt: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?... even so we also should walk in newness of life.
scripture.function: The theological explanation: baptism participates structurally in the gospel event itself — burial with Christ, resurrection to new life.

scripture.excerpt: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
scripture.function: Baptism as clothing with Christ — union with Christ is expressed through and sealed in baptism in apostolic doctrine.

scripture.excerpt: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God...
scripture.function: Baptism as the new-covenant counterpart to circumcision — the covenant entry rite that joins the believer to Christ’s death and resurrection.

scripture.excerpt: The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us... by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
scripture.function: Peter’s explicit statement that baptism saves — grounded in resurrection, not in the water itself, but in the covenantal appeal made to God through it.

scripture.excerpt: When they believed Philip preaching... they were baptized, both men and women...
scripture.function: The Samaritan pattern: belief followed by baptism followed by apostolic concern for Spirit reception — demonstrating the apostolic insistence on the full pattern.

vocabulary.definition: Baptism in water as commanded apostolic response to the gospel in relation to remission, burial with Christ, and covenant entry.
vocabulary.relevance: The central category of the domain — must be understood doctrinally rather than reduced to symbolic gesture or optional ceremony.

vocabulary.definition: The gospel category with which baptism is doctrinally associated in Romans 6 — baptism corresponds to Christ’s burial just as new life corresponds to His resurrection.
vocabulary.relevance: Grounds baptism in the gospel event itself; removes arbitrariness from the command.

vocabulary.definition: The release or forgiveness of sins according to divine provision — the specific result associated with baptism in Acts 2:38.
vocabulary.relevance: Makes baptism doctrinally significant rather than merely symbolic; remission is a real provision that accompanies real obedience.

vocabulary.definition: The cleansing category associated with baptismal response — Acts 22:16 and Titus 3:5 both use washing language in relation to baptism.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects baptism to the long biblical category of cleansing established in Domain 2.

vocabulary.definition: Entry into the publicly revealed covenant life of the gospel — baptism as the form in which new-covenant belonging is enacted.
vocabulary.relevance: Places baptism inside the covenant structure of Domain 2 — it is not external ceremony but the form of entry into a real relationship.

vocabulary.definition: Submission to the commanded practice of baptism as an act of faith and covenant response.
vocabulary.relevance: Frames baptism as obedience rather than ritual — the person being baptized is submitting to the authority of Christ and the apostolic proclamation.

vocabulary.definition: Baptismal action carried out in relation to the revealed name of Jesus Christ — the name that carries authority for remission and covenant entry.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects baptism to Domain 10’s treatment of the name of Jesus; explains why apostolic baptism is in Jesus’ name.

vocabulary.definition: The repeated practice and teaching of the apostles — baptism appears consistently in every major conversion account in Acts.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the normative force of baptism — its consistent presence in Acts is doctrinal evidence, not coincidence.

vocabulary.definition: The doctrinal relation between baptism and the burial dimension of the gospel — the believer is buried with Christ in baptism to rise with Him in new life.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives baptism its deepest theological meaning and connects it inseparably to the gospel event of Domain 3.

vocabulary.definition: The doctrinal seriousness and unity of Christian baptism — Ephesians 4:5 places it alongside one Lord and one faith.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that baptism cannot be treated as a matter of preference; its unity is as serious as the unity of the gospel.

domains.title: The Holy Spirit And The Necessity Of Spiritual Birth
domains.anchor: John 3:5 — "Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God."

scripture.excerpt: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed...
scripture.function: The promise of Spirit outpouring joined to blessing — a foretaste of the Joel prophecy and the Pentecost fulfillment.

scripture.excerpt: A new spirit will I put within you... I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes.
scripture.function: The prophetic promise of divine Spirit indwelling as the means of new life and obedience — the category that the new birth fulfills.

scripture.excerpt: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy...
scripture.function: The Joel promise Peter quotes at Pentecost (Acts 2:16–17) — establishing that the Spirit outpouring is the fulfillment of prophetic expectation.

scripture.excerpt: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
scripture.function: Christ’s own declaration of the necessity of Spirit birth — the most direct statement in the Gospels that the Spirit is essential to new-birth entry.

scripture.excerpt: He that believeth on me... out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (But this spake he of the Spirit...)
scripture.function: Christ’s promise of the Spirit to those who believe — establishing the Spirit as the interior spring of new-covenant life.

scripture.excerpt: ...ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off.
scripture.function: The Spirit is promised to all who respond to the apostolic command — establishing Spirit reception as part of the universal new-birth provision.

scripture.excerpt: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word...
scripture.function: The Gentile reception of the Spirit — confirming that Spirit birth crosses all boundaries and belongs to the one apostolic new-birth doctrine.

scripture.excerpt: If any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
scripture.function: Paul’s stark declaration: possession of the Spirit is the defining criterion of belonging to Christ — not profession, membership, or moral effort.

scripture.excerpt: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour.
scripture.function: Salvation by the Spirit’s renewal — the clearest Pauline statement that regeneration is a work of the Holy Spirit poured out abundantly through Christ.

scripture.excerpt: In whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance...
scripture.function: The Spirit as seal and earnest — Spirit reception is not only entry into covenant life but the divine guarantee of future inheritance.

vocabulary.definition: The Spirit of God given in new-covenant life — the same divine Spirit who inspired Scripture, raised Christ from the dead, and now indwells those born again.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the identity of what is received in the new birth — not an impersonal force or religious feeling but the Spirit of the living God.

vocabulary.definition: New life brought by God through His Spirit — the spiritual dimension of the new birth described by Christ in John 3:3–8.
vocabulary.relevance: Defines the necessity of the Spirit’s work; makes clear that the new birth requires more than moral reform or religious profession.

vocabulary.definition: God dwelling within His people by His Spirit — the fulfillment of the covenant promise of divine presence that runs through the Old Testament.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects Spirit reception to the divine-dwelling trajectory of Domain 2 — the Spirit is not an external influence but an interior presence.

vocabulary.definition: Renewal and new life brought by God through the Spirit — the making new of a person who was spiritually dead.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the depth of what Spirit birth accomplishes: not improvement but renewal of spiritual life from death to life.

vocabulary.definition: The promised Spirit given by God in covenant fulfillment — described in Acts 2:38 as the gift of the Holy Ghost, promised to all who repent and are baptized.
vocabulary.relevance: Frames Spirit reception as divine gift rather than human achievement; the Spirit is received, not earned.

vocabulary.definition: Birth from above by the Spirit — Christ’s own language in John 3 for the spiritual dimension of the new birth.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the vertical, divine origin of Spirit birth — it comes from above, not from within human nature.

vocabulary.definition: Inward transformation by divine action — the Spirit bringing newness of life, renewed mind, and changed orientation.
vocabulary.relevance: Distinguishes Spirit birth from external religion: renewal is inward, ongoing, and divinely initiated.

vocabulary.definition: The foretold gift of divine indwelling and power — promised by Joel, by Christ, and by Peter at Pentecost.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that Spirit reception is covenant fulfillment — not a new idea at Pentecost but the arrival of what God had long promised.

vocabulary.definition: Life lived through the gift and presence of the Spirit — the experiential reality of belonging to the new covenant.
vocabulary.relevance: Describes what the Christian life actually is: not rule-following but Spirit-indwelt living in the covenant God established.

vocabulary.definition: A gift essential to salvation, not merely an optional benefit — established by Christ’s own words in John 3:5 and Paul’s declaration in Romans 8:9.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents Spirit reception from being treated as a secondary experience available to some believers but not required for all.

domains.title: Pentecost And The Opening Of New-Covenant Birth
domains.anchor: Acts 2:1, 4 — "When the day of Pentecost was fully come... they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance."

scripture.excerpt: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy...
scripture.function: The prophetic foundation of the Pentecost outpouring — Peter quotes this text to establish that what is happening is fulfillment, not novelty.

scripture.excerpt: That repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations... I send the promise of my Father upon you...
scripture.function: Christ’s final words before ascension: the promise of the Spirit is connected to the apostolic proclamation of repentance and remission.

scripture.excerpt: Wait for the promise of the Father... ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence... ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you.
scripture.function: Christ’s final promise before ascension — Pentecost is explicitly awaited and anticipated as imminent fulfillment.

scripture.excerpt: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues... This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel...
scripture.function: The Pentecost event and Peter’s interpretation: fulfillment of Joel’s prophecy, publicly witnessed, leading immediately to apostolic proclamation.

scripture.excerpt: Jesus of Nazareth... Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
scripture.function: The Pentecost sermon: proclamation of Christ’s death, resurrection, and lordship leads to the commanded apostolic response.

scripture.excerpt: For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call.
scripture.function: The promise is universal and intergenerational — Pentecost opens new-birth entry to all people in every generation.

scripture.excerpt: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word... they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God.
scripture.function: The Gentile Pentecost — the same Spirit received at the original Pentecost (Acts 11:15–17), establishing that Pentecost is a pattern, not a one-time event.

scripture.excerpt: As I began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them, as on us at the beginning... God gave them the like gift as he did unto us...
scripture.function: Peter’s own interpretation of Cornelius’s Spirit reception: it matches Pentecost exactly. Pentecost establishes the normative pattern.

scripture.excerpt: He that believeth on me... out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (But this spake he of the Spirit...)
scripture.function: Christ’s own promise of the Spirit to those who believe — Pentecost is its fulfillment.

scripture.excerpt: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body...
scripture.function: The Spirit’s role in forming the one body — Pentecost opens not only individual Spirit birth but the formation of the apostolic covenant community.

vocabulary.definition: The public outpouring of the promised Spirit and the opening of new-covenant life — the event at which promise became fulfillment and proclamation became commanded response.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be interpreted as salvation-opening event and covenant turning point, not merely as a spectacular religious experience.

vocabulary.definition: The promised giving forth of God’s Spirit in abundance upon His people — poured out at Pentecost as the fulfillment of Joel’s prophecy.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that the Spirit is received, not generated — it is poured from above, not produced from within.

vocabulary.definition: The public beginning of revealed new-covenant life — the moment when the new covenant becomes available to all who respond to the apostolic proclamation.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives Pentecost its doctrinal weight: it is not only experiential but covenantal.

vocabulary.definition: An event in which prior promise and prophecy openly reach their promised realization.
vocabulary.relevance: Frames Pentecost within the covenant-promise trajectory of Domain 2 — it is not the beginning of something new but the arrival of what had been prepared.

vocabulary.definition: The beginning of public apostolic proclamation and commanded response — Pentecost is the day when the apostolic new-birth message is first proclaimed openly.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects Pentecost to the apostolic pattern of Domain 8 — everything in Acts 3–28 follows from what was opened at Pentecost.

vocabulary.definition: The beginning of the Spirit-empowered apostolic community formed by the gospel, the Spirit, and the commanded response.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects Pentecost to Domain 13’s treatment of the church.

vocabulary.definition: Observable manifestation marking fulfillment openly — the tongues and visible evidence that accompanied the Spirit’s outpouring at Pentecost.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that Pentecost was publicly verifiable, not merely inwardly felt.

vocabulary.definition: Spirit-born entry into the life opened at Pentecost — every subsequent new birth participates in what Pentecost opened.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes Pentecost not as a closed historical event but as the opening of an ongoing provision.

domains.title: The Apostolic Pattern Of The New Birth
domains.anchor: Acts 2:41 — "Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls."

scripture.excerpt: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
scripture.function: The inaugural pattern: repentance, baptism in Jesus’ name, remission, and Spirit reception all commanded in one apostolic proclamation.

scripture.excerpt: When they believed Philip preaching... they were baptized, both men and women. ...Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
scripture.function: The Samaritan pattern: belief and baptism followed by apostolic concern for Spirit reception — demonstrating that baptism alone was not treated as sufficient.

scripture.excerpt: And Ananias... said, Brother Saul... hath sent me, that thou mightest... be filled with the Holy Ghost. And immediately... he arose, and was baptized.
scripture.function: Paul’s own conversion: Spirit reception and water baptism both present — no account of Paul’s conversion omits either element.

scripture.excerpt: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word... he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.
scripture.function: The Gentile pattern: Spirit reception followed by water baptism — Peter commands water baptism even after the Spirit has fallen, establishing that Spirit reception does not make baptism unnecessary.

scripture.excerpt: What must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ... and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
scripture.function: The Philippian jailer: belief leads immediately to baptism — the urgency of the response reflects the apostolic seriousness of baptism.

scripture.excerpt: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?... the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
scripture.function: The Ephesian disciples: Paul’s immediate inquiry about Spirit reception shows that apostolic doctrine treated this as a known and expected element of new-birth entry.

scripture.excerpt: Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
scripture.function: Ananias’ command to Paul: baptism is urgent and directly tied to washing away sins — even Paul, who received a dramatic encounter with Christ, is commanded to be baptized.

scripture.excerpt: Philip... preached unto him Jesus. And as they went on their way... the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?
scripture.function: The Ethiopian eunuch: gospel preaching immediately produces the desire for baptism — apostolic preaching consistently produces this response.

scripture.excerpt: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body...
scripture.function: Paul’s theological summary: Spirit baptism and body membership are one — the new birth and church entry are not separate events.

scripture.excerpt: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
scripture.function: The Pauline theological summary of water baptism: it is the form in which the person puts on Christ — union with Christ is expressed and received in baptism.

vocabulary.definition: The consistent salvation-response pattern revealed in apostolic preaching and practice — repentance, baptism in Jesus’ name, and Spirit reception.
vocabulary.relevance: The domain’s central category: the pattern is not discovered by averaging the accounts but by reading them as doctrine in action.

vocabulary.definition: The recurring pattern of repentance, baptism, and Spirit reception seen across the major conversion accounts in Acts.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that the pattern is not incidental — it recurs across different settings, peoples, and preachers, establishing its doctrinal force.

vocabulary.definition: Practice that carries doctrinal force because it is repeated consistently in apostolic teaching and response.
vocabulary.relevance: Distinguishes apostolic practice from cultural preference — the repetition is evidence of doctrine, not coincidence.

vocabulary.definition: Repeated salvation response that reflects revealed doctrine rather than random variation.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents the learner from reading Acts accounts in isolation — the consistency across accounts is the doctrinal argument.

vocabulary.definition: A historical account in Acts showing how people responded to apostolic proclamation — each account is also doctrinal evidence.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that Acts is not only history but doctrine in narrative form.

vocabulary.definition: A pattern disclosed by God through repeated apostolic example and command — not a human tradition but a divine disclosure.
vocabulary.relevance: Places the apostolic pattern beyond the reach of cultural revision — it was revealed, not invented.

vocabulary.definition: Practice that expresses doctrine rather than personal preference — the apostles baptized in Jesus’ name and sought Spirit reception because these were doctrinal convictions.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the normative weight of practice — apostolic practice is evidence of apostolic doctrine.

vocabulary.definition: The response by which people enter new-covenant life — not a barrier but the form in which the gospel is received.
vocabulary.relevance: Frames the apostolic pattern as provision, not requirement.

vocabulary.definition: The unity of apostolic doctrine and practice across different settings — Jews, Samaritans, Gentiles, and later disciples all enter through the same new-birth pattern.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents the learner from reading different accounts as evidence of multiple salvation options.

vocabulary.definition: The revealed structure of response to the gospel — not a formula imposed by humans but the form God has established for entering new-covenant life.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the apostolic pattern to the full doctrinal structure of the new birth.

domains.title: Faith, Obedience, And Full Saving Response
domains.anchor: Hebrews 5:9 — "He became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him."

scripture.excerpt: He believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
scripture.function: The original statement of justification by faith — but Abraham’s faith expressed itself in obedient departure, covenant entry, and continued trust. Faith and obedience were never separated in the biblical model.

scripture.excerpt: The just shall live by his faith.
scripture.function: The foundational OT declaration of faith as the principle of righteous life — quoted three times in the NT to establish the continuity of faith-based living from Old to New Testament.

scripture.excerpt: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
scripture.function: The most famous faith-statement in Scripture — but its context (John 3:1–21) includes the necessity of new birth by water and Spirit, showing that believing and being born again are not alternatives.

scripture.excerpt: Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart... Then they that gladly received his word were baptized...
scripture.function: Faith receiving the word and responding in baptism — the Pentecost account shows that receiving the apostolic word means responding to its commands.

scripture.excerpt: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations...
scripture.function: Paul’s description of his apostolic mission: “obedience to the faith” — faith that is obeyed is the goal of apostolic proclamation.

scripture.excerpt: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered; And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him.
scripture.function: Eternal salvation is authored for those who obey — the obedience of faith is the form in which salvation is received.

scripture.excerpt: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen... By faith Abraham obeyed...
scripture.function: Hebrews 11 defines faith by its obedient acts — every example in the chapter is an act of obedient trust, not passive mental assent.

scripture.excerpt: Faith without works is dead... Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.
scripture.function: The apostolic distinction between living faith (which acts) and dead faith (which claims without obedience) — directly relevant to the relationship between faith and the apostolic new-birth pattern.

scripture.excerpt: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren...
scripture.function: Obedience to the truth produces purification — the form in which faith receives salvation is obedient response to the revealed truth of the gospel.

scripture.excerpt: If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall
scripture.function: Christ’s definition of discipleship: continuing in His word — faith is not a moment of assent but a continuing posture of obedience.

vocabulary.definition: Trust in God and His revealed truth — the disposition of the whole person toward God that receives His promises and responds to His commands.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be defined biblically rather than reduced to intellectual agreement or emotional feeling.

vocabulary.definition: Faith that responds obediently to God’s gospel and enters into revealed salvation — not a feeling or a decision only, but a trust that acts on what God has revealed.
vocabulary.relevance: Distinguishes the biblical concept of faith from modern reductions that separate belief from obedience.

vocabulary.definition: Faith expressed through obedient response to revelation — Paul’s phrase in Romans 1:5 and 16:26 that holds together faith and obedience as one reality.
vocabulary.relevance: Resolves the apparent tension: obedience is how biblical faith expresses itself, not a supplement added to faith.

vocabulary.definition: Agreement at the level of thought without full yielded response — a partial faith that knows truth without trusting God enough to act on it.
vocabulary.relevance: Names the reduction this domain is designed to correct.

vocabulary.definition: Dependence upon God and His saving work — faith understood as reliance rather than mere agreement.
vocabulary.relevance: Captures the relational dimension of saving faith.

vocabulary.definition: Faith that is active, responsive, and fruitful — the faith that James contrasts with dead faith.
vocabulary.relevance: Provides the positive standard against which dead faith is measured.

vocabulary.definition: Professed belief without obedient life or response — faith that claims to believe but refuses to respond to what God has revealed.
vocabulary.relevance: Names the danger this domain warns against.

vocabulary.definition: Obedience given in response to the gospel — the form in which faith receives what the gospel offers.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects faith and the apostolic new-birth pattern.

vocabulary.definition: God’s unearned favor and provision — the divine initiative that makes salvation possible, offered freely and received through faith.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents obedience from becoming merit; the standard teaches that obedient faith responds to grace rather than earning it.

vocabulary.definition: Belief that bows to divine authority — the kind of faith that not only knows what God has revealed but submits to it.
vocabulary.relevance: Captures the volitional dimension of saving faith.

domains.title: The Name Of Jesus In Salvation And Covenant Entry
domains.anchor: Acts 4:12 — "Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved."

scripture.excerpt: Ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD... I am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour.
scripture.function: The Old Testament declaration that the LORD alone is Savior — which the apostles apply to Jesus (Acts 4:12), establishing that the saving name of Jesus carries the full weight of the divine saving identity.

scripture.excerpt: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered.
scripture.function: The promise of salvation through calling on the divine name — which Peter applies to Jesus in Acts 2:21, establishing that calling on the name of Jesus is calling on the name of the LORD.

scripture.excerpt: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
scripture.function: The angel’s declaration that the name Jesus (Yeshua, “the LORD saves”) carries the saving content of the divine purpose — the name is not incidental but meaning-laden.

scripture.excerpt: That repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations.
scripture.function: Christ’s own commission: the content of apostolic proclamation (repentance and remission) is inseparable from the name in which it is preached.

scripture.excerpt: Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
scripture.function: Peter’s application of Joel’s promise to Jesus at Pentecost — establishing that the name of Jesus is the saving name through which Joel’s promise is fulfilled.

scripture.excerpt: ...be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins...
scripture.function: The inaugural apostolic command: baptism in Jesus’ name for remission of sins — the name is the covenantal authority under which baptismal response takes place.

scripture.excerpt: By the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth... neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
scripture.function: The most definitive New Testament statement of the exclusive saving significance of the name of Jesus.

scripture.excerpt: To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.
scripture.function: All prophetic witness converges on remission through the name of Jesus — establishing that the name’s saving significance is not apostolic invention but the fulfillment of prophetic testimony.

scripture.excerpt: God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow...
scripture.function: The post-resurrection exaltation of the name of Jesus — the name that is above every name is the name invoked in apostolic salvation response.

scripture.excerpt: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
scripture.function: The comprehensive apostolic principle: everything done by believers is done in the name of Jesus — the name is the authority structure of all apostolic life and practice.

vocabulary.definition: The revealed saving name of Jesus Christ invoked in apostolic proclamation and response — not a verbal formula but the declaration of the saving identity and authority of Jesus.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be understood doctrinally and relationally, not merely linguistically.

vocabulary.definition: The name attached to divine salvation and covenant response — Acts 4:12 declares that no other name has saving power.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes the exclusive significance of Jesus’ name in salvation doctrine.

vocabulary.definition: The revealed power and right associated with the name of Jesus — the authority given by God to the exalted Christ (Phil. 2:9–11).
vocabulary.relevance: Explains why baptism in Jesus’ name is not superstition — it is submission to the authority that God has placed in that name.

vocabulary.definition: Calling upon the name in faith, obedience, appeal, or confession — the apostolic form of engaging the saving power of Christ.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the name to the experiential dimension of salvation.

vocabulary.definition: The revealed name associated with entry into apostolic salvation response — the name in which baptism is administered and remission received.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives the name its place in the new-birth structure: it is the covenantal form of entry into Christ.

vocabulary.definition: Public acknowledgment of Jesus in revealed identity and authority — the confession that Jesus is Lord (Rom. 10:9–13).
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the name to the obedience of faith.

vocabulary.definition: Authority openly disclosed by God in the saving name of Jesus — not human tradition but divine revelation.
vocabulary.relevance: Grounds the significance of the name in divine action rather than human tradition.

vocabulary.definition: Response made under and in relation to the name of Jesus — the form in which apostolic salvation response is enacted.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains why the name appears in repentance proclamation, baptismal command, and Spirit invocation in apostolic practice.

domains.title: Remission, Cleansing, And Covenant Application
domains.anchor: Acts 2:38 — "...be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins..."

scripture.excerpt: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow... Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
scripture.function: David’s prayer for cleansing establishes washing and heart renewal as categories that reach fulfillment in the new birth.

scripture.excerpt: Wash you, make you clean... though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
scripture.function: God’s invitation to washing and cleansing as the form of restoration — the scarlet/white imagery prepared the category that apostolic doctrine applies to new-birth cleansing.

scripture.excerpt: He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.
scripture.function: The prophetic basis of remission: Christ bears iniquities so that many may be justified — the ground of all apostolic remission teaching.

scripture.excerpt: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.
scripture.function: The messianic promise of an opened fountain for cleansing — a direct anticipation of the new-covenant application categories of remission and washing.

scripture.excerpt: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
scripture.function: Christ’s own institution of the connection between His blood and remission of sins — the doctrinal ground of all apostolic remission proclamation.

scripture.excerpt: Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins...
scripture.function: The first apostolic command attaching remission to baptism in Jesus’ name — the application of Christ’s blood-remission to the believer through the commanded response.

scripture.excerpt: To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.
scripture.function: All prophetic witness converges on remission through the name of Jesus — establishing remission as the fulfillment of the entire prophetic testimony.

scripture.excerpt: Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
scripture.function: The explicit washing language in the baptismal command — establishes that the washing category belongs to the baptismal act.

scripture.excerpt: And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.
scripture.function: The triple application — washed, sanctified, justified — all through the name of Jesus and by the Spirit. Washing belongs to salvation application alongside sanctification and justification.

scripture.excerpt: The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin... If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
scripture.function: The ongoing dimension of cleansing: the blood continues to cleanse as we walk in the light — remission and cleansing are not only entry categories but ongoing covenant realities.

vocabulary.definition: Forgiveness or release from sins according to divine provision — the doctrinal category attached to baptism in Jesus’ name in apostolic proclamation.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be understood doctrinally and not reduced to a vague sense of being forgiven.

vocabulary.definition: Washing away of defilement and guilt according to God’s redemptive work — applied to the believer through the new- birth response.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the preparatory categories of Domain 2 to their apostolic application in the new birth.

vocabulary.definition: Cleansing language associated with salvation application — Acts 22:16 commands washing away of sins in the baptismal context.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives specific scriptural grounding to the cleansing category; the washing is not metaphor only but the apostolic description of what happens in new-birth response.

vocabulary.definition: The way God’s saving provision is applied within the revealed response — remission and cleansing as the form in which the gospel’s benefits become real in the believer’s life.
vocabulary.relevance: Frames remission and cleansing as the application dimension of salvation.

vocabulary.definition: The removal of guilt according to divine mercy and justice — the relational dimension of remission.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents remission from being merely juridical; forgiveness is also relational restoration.

vocabulary.definition: The actual application of Christ’s saving work to the believer — remission, cleansing, and justification as the personal reception of what Christ accomplished.
vocabulary.relevance: Distinguishes the objective gospel event (what Christ did) from its subjective application (what is received through faith and obedience).

vocabulary.definition: The removal of uncleanness in relation to God — the comprehensive category that includes both remission of guilt and cleansing of defilement.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that salvation addresses both guilt (the legal problem) and defilement (the relational problem).

vocabulary.definition: Inward cleansing in relation to guilt and approach to God (Heb. 10:22) — the experiential dimension of remission and washing in the new birth.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the external categories of cleansing and washing to their inward effect.

domains.title: Spirit Reception, Signs, And New-Covenant
domains.anchor: Acts 2:4 — "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance."

scripture.excerpt: With stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people... yet they would not hear.
scripture.function: The prophetic anticipation of a Spirit-given speech mark attached to God’s covenant work — Paul applies this in 1 Corinthians 14:21 to the tongues phenomenon.

scripture.excerpt: Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit.
scripture.function: The promise of Spirit outpouring with prophetic manifestation — fulfilled at Pentecost and the basis for the sign dimension of Spirit reception.

scripture.excerpt: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
scripture.function: The inaugural Spirit reception: tongues as the Spirit gives utterance is the initial evidence of Spirit fullness at Pentecost — establishing the pattern for subsequent Spirit reception.

scripture.excerpt: Therefore being by the right hand of God exalted, and having received of the Father the promise of the Holy Ghost, he hath shed forth this, which ye now see and hear.
scripture.function: Peter connects the observable sign (what you see and hear) to the exalted Christ pouring out the Spirit — the sign points to the source and confirms the event.

scripture.excerpt: When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given... he offered them money.
scripture.function: Simon observed something when the Spirit was given — the sign was recognizable to an outsider, establishing that Spirit reception had observable dimensions the apostles expected.

scripture.excerpt: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word... For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God.
scripture.function: The Gentile reception: the apostles knew the Gentiles had received the Spirit because they heard them speak with tongues — tongues is explicitly the evidence by which Spirit reception was recognized.

scripture.excerpt: As I began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them, as on us at the beginning.
scripture.function: Peter’s account of the Cornelius event: the Spirit fell on the Gentiles exactly as on the 120 at the beginning — establishing that Gentile Spirit reception matched the Pentecost pattern.

scripture.excerpt: When Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
scripture.function: The Ephesian disciples: tongues accompanied Spirit reception, confirming the Pentecostal pattern far removed from Jerusalem.

scripture.excerpt: God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
scripture.function: Spirit reception produces the cry of covenant relationship — the Spirit’s presence is identifiable by its covenantal expression.

scripture.excerpt: In whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed
scripture.function: The Spirit as seal and earnest of the covenant inheritance — Spirit reception

vocabulary.definition: Receiving the Holy Spirit in new-covenant salvation — the fulfillment of the divine promise of indwelling that belongs to new-birth entry.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be understood as both doctrinal category and experiential reality within the new-birth structure.

vocabulary.definition: Outwardly evident sign accompanying Spirit reception — specifically tongues as the Spirit gives utterance in the Pentecostal pattern.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that Spirit reception in apostolic doctrine is not purely invisible; the apostles recognized and expected observable dimensions.

vocabulary.definition: Authoritative testimony concerning what the apostles recognized and proclaimed regarding Spirit reception.
vocabulary.relevance: Grounds the sign dimension in apostolic authority; the tongues sign is doctrinally significant because the apostles treated it as significant.

vocabulary.definition: The observable aspect attached to Spirit reception texts in Acts — tongues as the initial evidence the apostles recognized.
vocabulary.relevance: Names the specific manifestation connected to Spirit reception in the apostolic pattern.

vocabulary.definition: Public identification as belonging to the Spirit-born people of God — the sign as the means by which Spirit reception was recognized.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains why the sign matters: it publicly identifies the receiver as one who has entered new-covenant life through the Spirit.

vocabulary.definition: The evidence by which Spirit reception is recognized in apostolic witness — tongues as the Spirit gives utterance in the Acts pattern.
vocabulary.relevance: Grounds the doctrine of initial evidence in the apostolic accounts.

vocabulary.definition: Outward expression of inward spiritual reception — the Spirit making itself known through observable means.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents the sign from being dismissed as irrelevant while maintaining that the sign points to the Spirit rather than replacing focus on the Spirit.

vocabulary.definition: The apostolic acknowledgment that the Spirit has been received — based on the observable evidence the apostles recognized (Acts 10:46–47).
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes why the sign matters pastorally: it allows the believer and the community to recognize and confirm Spirit reception.

domains.title: The New Birth And Entry Into The Church
domains.anchor: Acts 2:47 — "...the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved."

scripture.excerpt: Ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people... a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.
scripture.function: The Old Testament covenant-people identity — which 1 Peter 2:9–10 applies to the new-covenant church, establishing continuity between Israel’s covenant identity and the apostolic community.

scripture.excerpt: I will make a new covenant... I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
scripture.function: The promise of a covenant people — “they shall be my people” is corporate, not only individual. The new birth brings people into a new-covenant people.

scripture.excerpt: I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
scripture.function: Christ’s own declaration that He is building a church — not a loose spiritual network but a defined community.

scripture.excerpt: They that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
scripture.function: The first new-birth community: baptism is immediately followed by addition to the community and continuation in apostolic doctrine, fellowship, worship, and prayer. New birth and church life are inseparable.

scripture.excerpt: For as the body is one, and hath many members... For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body...
scripture.function: The theological explanation of church membership: Spirit baptism incorporates believers into one body. The Spirit-born community is one body under one Head.

scripture.excerpt: Ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.
scripture.function: The comprehensive description of church membership: new-birth entry makes a person a citizen, household member, and stone in a building — all corporate identities.

scripture.excerpt: There is one body, and one Spirit... one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all.
scripture.function: The seven unities: the doctrine of the church is built on doctrinal unity — the same unities established in the new-birth pattern.

scripture.excerpt: Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people... which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God.
scripture.function: The new-covenant application of the Exodus covenant-people language: the church is a covenant people formed by the gospel and the Spirit.

scripture.excerpt: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together...
scripture.function: The apostolic expectation that new-birth entry includes continued assembly and mutual accountability.

scripture.excerpt: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me,
scripture.function: Christ’s prayer for the unity of believers — the covenant community is defined by

vocabulary.definition: The apostolic community of people brought into covenant life through the gospel — not a building or organization but the Spirit-formed people of God.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be defined ecclesiologically, not culturally; the church is what new-birth entry creates.

vocabulary.definition: The gathered people of God joined in one spiritual life and identity under Christ — the corporate reality into which Spirit baptism incorporates believers.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects Spirit reception (Domain 12) to church membership: one Spirit → one body (1 Cor. 12:13).

vocabulary.definition: The people formed under God’s new-covenant life and order — the community into which new-birth entry brings the believer.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives the church its theological definition: it is a covenant community, not a voluntary association.

vocabulary.definition: Shared life under apostolic doctrine, worship, prayer, and spiritual unity — the ongoing life of the community established in Acts 2:42–47.
vocabulary.relevance: Describes what the community actually does: continues in apostolic doctrine, breaking of bread, prayer, and fellowship.

vocabulary.definition: Entrance into the apostolic people of God through new-birth response — not a separate step after salvation but the communal dimension of the new birth itself.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that church membership is not optional post- salvation enrollment but part of what the new birth creates.

vocabulary.definition: Shared life in Christ by the Spirit among believers — the spiritual reality of the one body.
vocabulary.relevance: Grounds church unity in the Spirit rather than in organizational structure.

vocabulary.definition: The outwardly identifiable gathered people of God — the church that can be seen, identified, and added to.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that the church is not invisible only; Acts 2:41 says the Lord added to the church.

vocabulary.definition: A community ordered by revealed teaching, not mere religious preference — the church that continues in the apostles’ doctrine (Acts 2:42).
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents the church from being redefined as any gathering of spiritual people.

vocabulary.definition: The defined life and belonging of those brought into apostolic covenant community — citizen, household member, stone in the building, member of the body.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives the learner multiple scriptural images of what church membership means.

vocabulary.definition: The unity of the church as one people under one gospel, one Spirit, one baptism, and one Lord — the doctrinal unity established in Ephesians 4:4–6.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects the new-birth doctrine of Domains 1–12 to the ecclesiology of Domain 13.

domains.title: The New Birth And Transformed Living
domains.anchor: II Corinthians 5:17 — "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new."

scripture.excerpt: Ye shall be holy: for I am holy.
scripture.function: The Old Testament foundation of holiness: God’s people are called to holiness because He is holy. 1 Peter 1:15–16 applies this directly to new-covenant believers — holiness is grounded in God’s nature.

scripture.excerpt: A new spirit will I put within you... I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes.
scripture.function: The promise of Spirit indwelling as the means of obedient living — transformed living is not self-generated effort but the fruit of the Spirit within.

scripture.excerpt: Ye are the salt of the earth... Ye are the light of the world... Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
scripture.function: Christ’s description of the transformed life of His people — visible goodness that glorifies God in the world.

scripture.excerpt: Yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead... For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
scripture.function: The apostolic call to yield the newborn life entirely to God — transformed living as the expression of the life received in the new birth.

scripture.excerpt: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice... be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.
scripture.function: The comprehensive apostolic call to transformed living: non-conformity to the world and renewal of mind as the shape of new-covenant life.

scripture.excerpt: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh... The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance.
scripture.function: The Spirit as the means and source of transformed living — fruit of the Spirit as the evidence of Spirit-born life.

scripture.excerpt: This I say therefore... that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk... And that ye put on the new man.
scripture.function: The Pauline contrast between pre-conversion and post-conversion life — putting off the old and putting on the new as the ongoing practice of the new-birth community.

scripture.excerpt: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above... Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth...
scripture.function: Resurrection life applied to daily conduct: because the believer has been raised with Christ (new birth), they set their affection on things above.

scripture.excerpt: For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.
scripture.function: Grace teaches transformed living — holiness is not the alternative to grace but its fruit.

scripture.excerpt: Be sober, and hope to the end for the grace... As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts... Be ye holy; for I am holy.
scripture.function: Peter’s call to holy living grounded in the divine nature and the gospel — holiness is the appropriate response of those who have received the mercy of new-birth salvation.

vocabulary.definition: Life changed by the reality of salvation and the work of the Spirit — not self-improvement but new life expressing itself in holy conduct.
vocabulary.relevance: Must be understood as fruit of the new birth rather than its cause or condition.

vocabulary.definition: Separation unto God in life, conduct, and devotion — grounded in God’s own holiness and expressed in the life of the new-birth community.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents transformed living from being reduced to cultural conformity or personal preference.

vocabulary.definition: Submitted response to God’s will in continuing life — not the cause of salvation but its natural expression in the life of the Spirit-born.
vocabulary.relevance: Connects transformed living to the obedience-of-faith theme of Domain 9.

vocabulary.definition: The visible moral and spiritual result of Spirit-governed life (Gal. 5:22–23) — the character of Christ formed in the Spirit-born believer.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes that transformed character is Spirit-produced, not human-manufactured.

vocabulary.definition: Life progressively ordered under God in purity and devotion — the ongoing work of the Spirit in the new-birth community.
vocabulary.relevance: Gives theological definition to the process of transformed living.

vocabulary.definition: Life lived under the rule, values, and order of God — the new- birth community existing as a counter-culture ordered by the kingdom.
vocabulary.relevance: Establishes why transformed living involves separation from the world — not as cultural preference but as kingdom allegiance.

vocabulary.definition: Ongoing shaping of the believer by the Word and Spirit — the process by which the new-birth community grows into the image of Christ.
vocabulary.relevance: Prevents transformed living from being treated as only initial conversion change.

vocabulary.definition: Distinctness from sin and worldliness because of belonging to God — not cultural isolationism but moral distinctness grounded in divine identity.
vocabulary.relevance: Explains the separation principle: the new-birth community is distinct from the world not by withdrawal but by belonging to God.
